name: navigator-session-isolation
body:
The distributed `codebase-navigator` prompt bounds subagent session reuse: every `task` dispatch is a fresh, ISOLATED subagent session (with `task_id` absent), one dispatch = one self-contained unit of work, and starting a new task is ALWAYS a new dispatch. The ONLY permitted resume is the tight hand-back loop within ONE dispatch: the subagent returns needing a navigator action (a scan, a quick verify, an `apg_review_action`), the navigator performs it, and resumes THAT SAME session only to finish the SAME task (e.g. mark it done via `apg_plan_done` + `apg_plan_note`), then ends it.

Acceptance criteria (all observable in `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`, pinned by the coherence test):
1. The prompt states each `task` dispatch is a fresh, isolated subagent session with `task_id` absent; one dispatch = one self-contained unit of work; a new task is always a new dispatch.
2. It states the one permitted resume — the same-dispatch hand-back loop (subagent returns needing a navigator action → the navigator performs it → resume that same session to finish the same task → end it).
3. It states resumption serves only to finish the same task: it starts different tasks zero times, resumes a reviewer zero times (each review round is a fresh dispatch), and carries across phases zero times.
4. It states the motivation: subagent context is finite; repeatedly resumed sessions accumulate context until they break; isolation is the design.
5. The "Resume the same session, only to mark done" step (the Implementation-flow bullet) is scoped to this bounded hand-back rather than a general licence.
6. The coherence e2e test `rust.main_e2e.e2e.coordinator_agent_carries_review_action_and_dispatch_prose` asserts the isolation prose so it holds fast against silent regression.

Scope/non-goals: the product-source prompt plus the test only; zero binary behaviour change; zero other `opencode-suite/agents/*` file edited; the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts and sit outside this requirement.
